images.title: Take 2 from every value, the mean drops by 2
images.purpose: Shows the algebra: each of n values loses 2, the sum loses 2n, and dividing by n gives a − 2.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Three lines of working stacked in the centre, joined by two short downward arrows.
images.exact_structure: Three rounded rectangles stacked vertically and centred, joined by two short dark downward arrows. Top rectangle: the expression (x1 − 2) + (x2 − 2) + … + (xn − 2), with each “− 2” drawn in vermilion ({negative}) and the rest in dark text; the 1, 2 and n are small subscripts. Middle rectangle: = sum − 2n, with “− 2n” in vermilion. The arrow from the middle to the bottom rectangle carries the small label ÷ n. Bottom rectangle, larger and outlined in reddish purple ({focus}): new mean = a − 2. Every minus is a true minus sign. No other text, no dots, no graph.

images.takeaway: Taking 2 off every value takes exactly 2 off the mean, not 2n.
images.description: Shows the algebra: each of n values loses 2, the sum loses 2n, and dividing by n gives a − 2.
images.context: n values with mean a; subtract 2 from each.
images.teaching_notes: Targets the slip of thinking the mean drops by 2 times the number of values.

image_decisions.why: The three line chain makes the algebra step from sum to mean visible in one glance.
